input.text: Welcome to Olympic Green — Beijing's monument to its two Olympic Games, two thousand eight and two thousand twenty-two — the only city on Earth to host both the Summer and Winter editions. Before you rises the Bird's Nest — the National Stadium — its tangled steel lattice designed by architects Herzog & de Meuron with artist Ai Weiwei as consultant. It cost years of engineering to make randomness look effortless: every beam is placed, none is decor. Beside it, the glowing blue cube is the Water Cube — the National Aquatics Center, where swimming world records famously fell like dominoes in two thousand eight — and which was later transformed, astonishingly, into the "Ice Cube" curling venue for the Winter Games. At night the whole park lights up — the nest glows red, the cube shimmers blue, and families fly kites on the great axis between them. Come after sunset: this is Beijing's modern skyline of dreams, and it photographs best in the dark.
